title: perf(sessions): keep cleanup responsive and reuse workers

commit.messageHeadline: perf(sessions): reduce disk-pressure reclamation overhead
refactor(sessions): keep reclamation contracts acyclic
fix(sessions): preserve current admission during sweep worker reuse
test(gateway): align reclamation probe with worker bootstrap
fix(sessions): preserve cold mutation lifetimes during sweep reuse
test(auto-reply): incorporate canonical thinking test split
perf(sessions): retain the verified reclamation worker
refactor(sessions): clarify reclamation cleanup handling
test: drain retained database workers before fixture cleanup
test: preserve fixture state through retained worker drainage
chore: merge current main into reclamation fix
test: adapt archive bootstrap proof to tsdown handle
test(sessions): drain archive fixture resources before removal
test(gateway): drain the captured shared-state fixture owner
Merge commit 'd569fcdba8bd04b9ae6787af432a6fef409cade7' into codex/re…
fix(gateway): yield to I/O between startup phases
perf(sessions): trim archive worker database bootstrap
perf(sessions): skip artifact preparation without file candidates
perf(state): keep startup agent integrity scans off the main thread
fix(sessions): preserve validation ownership across worker reuse
perf(sessions): reuse scoped archive workers during cleanup
refactor(sessions): isolate archive contracts from execution
fix(sessions): preserve worker write reservations
fix(state): remove obsolete database resource export
fix(sessions): preserve worker reuse across preflight integration
perf(sessions): yield between cleanup phases

Codex review: blocked before merge. _Reviewed September 13, 2026, 7:45 AM ET / 11:45 UTC (Revision 29)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Session cleanup reuses bounded background workers, avoids redundant metadata processing, and moves startup integrity scans off the Gateway thread while preserving archive and deletion ordering. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 5 items remain** Keep open: this remains useful, maintainer-backed work that current main does not replace. The updated MASSIVE evidence resolves the previous performance blocker, and source review found no blocking correctness defect. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `d49a43e01bf8db330560b7a2f1258bcf733b68c5` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Strong runtime evidence and coherent lifecycle ownership support a good patch rating; published-updater acceptance remains the merge blocker. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): The captured body’s current-build Linux Gateway SMOKE, SCALE, and MASSIVE runs exercise the changed cleanup workers with concurrent reads, archive conservation, and observed native shutdown; MASSIVE now passes. This preserves the runtime proof classification while the separately required published-updater handoff remains pending. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): The captured body’s current-build Linux Gateway SMOKE, SCALE, and MASSIVE runs exercise the changed cleanup workers with concurrent reads, archive conservation, and observed native shutdown; MASSIVE now passes. This preserves the runtime proof classification while the separately required published-updater handoff remains pending. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Accepted lifecycle design: The September 12 design decision explicitly accepts one retained reclamation worker, per-operation authority and settlement, 60-second idle retirement, and joined native shutdown; it also requires published-driver update compatibility. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140897#issuecomment-5647899202.
Current main still uses per-operation workers: Fetched main still calls the one-shot archive-worker operation for reclamation and publishes after native exit. The retained worker architecture remains a distinct contribution beyond the merged admission and offline-cleanup repairs.
Latest-release comparison: The v2026.9.4 source also uses per-operation worker reclamation. The local release blob could not be retrieved through Git’s promisor remote, so the source was inspected through GitHub’s contents API. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together OpenClaw’s session storage handles cleanup and deletion requests against per-agent SQLite databases. It protects retained conversations, archives eligible transcripts, commits removals, and publishes results back to Gateway and CLI callers. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Cleanup or deletion request] --> B[Check current session protections] B --> C[Scoped archive worker] C --> D[Retained deletion worker] D --> E[Recheck authority and commit] E --> F[Publish durable results] D --> G[Drain on retirement or shutdown] C --> G ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The actual published 2026.9.4 updater restart handoff remains unverified for this build; retained workers must drain without preventing restart or leaving database leases behind. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The source-runtime measurements show higher immediate RSS, including after drainage; sustained memory cost on smaller hosts remains uncharacterized. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Complete the actual published 2026.9.4 updater restart handoff on the validated build, confirming retained-worker exit, released leases, preserved state, and healthy restart. - [ ] **Review config compatibility** - Confirm compatibility and upgrade impact for the changed config or default surface before merge. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge.
Agent review details ### Security None. ### PR surface PR surface statistics unavailable: the file list is incomplete. ### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus test growth** | Production net +1,475 lines; tests/support net +1,864 lines | Production growth implements the accepted worker reuse, admission, and retirement lifecycle rather than new configuration or storage formats. | | **Current-build MASSIVE acceptance** | 56m21.895s; maximum lifetime gap 477.838 ms | Both the unchanged 60-minute budget and 500 ms responsiveness limit now pass. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `unknown-truncated-pull-files`. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Finish the accepted updater check (recommended)** Complete the published 2026.9.4 restart handoff against the validated build, showing retained-worker drainage, state preservation, and healthy restart. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep bounded reuse within the existing storage owner, with published-updater compatibility established before landing and the measured memory tradeoff retained in the evidence. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes for repeated worker startup: current main visibly creates a worker for each reclamation, and the supplied paired workloads exercise that path. Exact latency on fetched main was not reproduced in this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes: the patch extends the existing archive and reclamation owners, preserves per-victim transactions and live guards, and supplies current-build performance evidence; updater acceptance remains outstanding. Maintainer design decision: extend the reusable reclamation owner in this PR to retain at most one verified reclamation Worker and one admitted agent database connection per Gateway process, with 60-second idle retirement. This addresses repeated full integrity scans between individual cleanup operations. The existing per-sweep implementation is the starting point; there must be one reclamation owner after the cutover.

The accepted boundaries are:

- Preserve the global lifecycle-archive FIFO and materialized-byte limits. Reuse only for the exact canonical database and shared-state owner; switching databases first drains, closes and joins the old Worker. Do not batch deletion transactions or retain queued plans in an idle Worker.
- Every physical writable open still performs full integrity, foreign-key, owner, schema and canonical-index admission. Reuse is a retained physical connection, never a cached health verdict after close.
- Each operation obtains a fresh numbered writer admission, checks the live lease and parent authority, rereads target/protection predicates in its own transaction, and uses its own commit gate. Publish results and release admission only after the matching operation settlement. Native exit remains mandatory proof of connection retirement.
- Cancellation before commit unwinds admission; after authorization, completion joins settlement. Crash or uncertain settlement retires the actor without replaying a possibly committed mutation. Lease cleanup requires the exact Worker-bound receipt and a joined native exit.
- Agent deletion, quarantine, database replacement/maintenance, owner-root changes and shutdown revoke reuse and drain the actor before proceeding. Idle close failures remain visible and retryable through the existing close owner. CLI shutdown drains immediately.
- Archive publication, pressure measurement, oldest-first retention and native harness deletion callbacks keep their current owners and ordering. No new schema, persisted representation, configuration option, retention policy or transaction batching is accepted.

Rollback drains the retained owner before restoring one-shot execution; no data conversion is needed. Required proof includes real SQLite/Worker before-and-after scan counts and timing, per-entry archive byte equality, cross-database isolation, idle reopen, append concurrency, stale/protected targets, authority revocation, postcommit cancellation, crash/failed close, deletion/maintenance/quarantine, shutdown and published-driver update compatibility. Existing failed performance observations remain failures; this decision does not waive the recorded stress acceptance thresholds.

Related: #112423. This records the accepted storage-lifecycle design for the implementing update; it is not a claim that implementation or validation is complete.
